title: Expressly conditional acceptance
summary: An expressly conditional response makes the responder’s willingness to contract depend on the offeror’s assent to additional or different terms. Under § 2-207(1), that can prevent the response from operating as acceptance.
notes:
Dorton requires a clear indication that the responder is unwilling to proceed without that assent; merely saying the transaction is subject to a form’s terms did not suffice there. C. Itoh uses language that does satisfy the condition, but subsequent performance creates a contract under subsection (3) without the unagreed arbitration clause. Distinguish agreement to transact from agreement to the contested term. Also distinguish a conditional acceptance from an offer that limits acceptance to its own terms under subsection (2)(a).

Dorton requires a clear indication that the offeree is unwilling to proceed without assurance of assent, and rejects mere “subject to” language on those forms. C. Itoh uses an explicit condition, but later performance forms a contract under subsection (3) without the unmatched arbitration term. Klocek finds an inadequate showing of conditional acceptance under the possible standards it considers. An effective formation-blocking condition does not by itself secure the desired substantive term.
